text:
alex: Heads up — ran into an odd case while testing the new credential surface: requests from legacy api keys end up with org=null in the attribution pipeline. Not sure how the console should display that.
maria: Ugh. Is that the keys minted before we introduced project-bound keys? I thought we defaulted those to org-level.
jin: Correct, legacy keys are effectively ownerless at the project level. We retro-tagged many but not all. Some customers keep the raw key in infra and never set a project.
sam: For telemetry, we currently mark those as project:unknown and attribute cost to org_unknown. That breaks per-project dashboards.
leila: From a UX standpoint we can show a banner: "Key not tied to a project — set a project for better billing and SLOs" with a button to assign. But we need to be sure we don't surface anything sensitive.
alex: Implementation question: do we prefer automatic migration (assign to org's default project) or a nudge (UI+api) so owner explicitly chooses? Auto-migration is simpler but could mis-attribute historical usage.
jin: Historical attribution is the sticky bit. If we reassign, we should keep a historical attribute map so past events still show old 'unassigned' state in evals. We could add an attribution_version field on events.
maria: That attribution_version idea seems clean. It lets us backfill without rewriting time-series. Telemetry pipeline would accept events with attribute_version=1 (legacy) or 2 (migrated). Then dashboards pick which to show.
sam: Perf/implementation note: adding a small enum to the event envelope is cheap. The bigger work is the console filter: allow "include legacy unassigned" toggle.
leila: Also need to consider quota enforcement: should unassigned keys be subject to org-level quotas only? We risk letting someone bypass project quotas.
alex: My vote is org-level quotas for unassigned, and block project-level SLA features until assigned. That avoids silent bypass.
jin: Agree. And we should add a short grace window (30d) where we email owners to assign before we auto-assign to a default project.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: attribution_version v2 pipeline will be rolled out to staging at 2025-03-04T09:00Z. Watch telemetry: /alerts/attribution-backfill failing if >1% mismatch.
maria: For the API change, expose a PATCH /keys/:id/assign_project with a dry_run flag and reason. Include audit log entry.
alex: Good. Let's file two small tickets: one for pipeline envelope change + backfill plan, one for console UX + assign API + email flow. I'll take the pipeline ticket.
sam: I'll pick the console + email flow. I'll add a mockup with wording that avoids exposing raw key value.
leila: I'll draft the email content and the 30d policy language for legal review.
jin: One more: metrics we should track — percent of active requests with project=unknown, migration acceptance rate, quota-block events for unassigned keys. Add those to the rollouts dashboard.
alex: Thanks team. Quick follow-up: do we want to surface assignment in the SDKs (helper function) or keep it console/API only?
maria: SDK helper is nice but not necessary for v1. We'll add a helper in devex after we see adoption.
ops-bot: note: production rollout gated on alert threshold and manual signoff from eng-platform leads.
alex: Cool. I'll create the two tickets and link them here.
